newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Nov budget deficit down, target to be met.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Nov budget deficit down, target to be met.

text.p: Canada's federal budget deficit fell C$618 million in November from C$1.64 billion a year earlier, the Finance Department said on Friday.
For the fiscal year to date, April to November, the deficit totalled C$8.12 billion, down from C$19.26 billion in the same period a year earlier.

The results to date cannot be used to extrapolate what the deficit for the whole year will be, since part of the improvement was attributable to developments unique to the first quarter and other factors. But the department voiced optimism the C$24.3 billion full-year target would be met.
"The deficit results to date clearly suggest that the deficit target for 1996-97 will be met and possibly bettered," the department said in its monthly Fiscal Monitor.
The department said the improvement for November reflected C$590 million less in program spending, C$260 million less in public debt charges and C$174 million more in revenues.
The improvement for the year to date was due mainly to a 7.4 percent increase in budgetary revenues -- mainly because of strong growth in income taxes -- and a 5.8 percent fall in program spending.
(Note: Positive numbers indicate net source of funds. Negative numbers indicate net requirement for funds.)
Yr to date 96/97 Yr to date 95/96
